answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a bond inside a shared atlas of verified identities before it can trade. The kernel of the defense is that the bond is locked and slashed on fraud, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must fund each one and loses the stake when any is caught. A plume of cheap fake identities collapses because creating them costs real capital while honest agents keep their bond and reputation.
